objective_for_doctor:
Age: 51
Sex: F
Chief Complaint: pain

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I have a burning sensation that starts in my stomach then goes up into my throat, sometimes with a bitter taste in my mouth. I also have pain in my lower and upper chest and epigastric area, and my symptoms get worse after eating.
What is your age, and do you have any cardiac risk factors such as hypertension, diabetes, high cholesterol, smoking history, or family history of early heart disease?
Does the pain occur with physical exertion or only after eating, and does it improve with antacids or when you sit upright?
It happens mainly after eating, and I don’t know if it improves with antacids or when I sit upright.
Does the chest pain radiate to your arm, jaw, back, or shoulder, and is it ever accompanied by shortness of breath, sweating, or nausea?
No—my pain only radiates to my lower chest. I don’t know about shortness of breath, sweating, or nausea.
How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any difficulty swallowing, painful swallowing, or unintentional weight loss?
I don't know how long I’ve been experiencing them. I don’t know if I have difficulty swallowing, painful swallowing, or unintentional weight loss.
Do your symptoms worsen when you lie down or bend over, and do they ever wake you up at night?
Have you noticed any vomiting, black or tarry stools, or blood in your vomit?
Do you take medications like ibuprofen, aspirin, or blood thinners, and do spicy or acidic foods trigger your symptoms?
I’m not sure about those triggers or medications. But I do have a hiatal hernia, and my symptoms get worse after eating. I also smoke cigarettes.
[DDX] Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), Acute coronary syndrome/Angina pectoris, Peptic ulcer disease, Esophageal spasm, Biliary colic
